items.title: Antisolvent chloride example
paragraphs: The room-temperature DMSO/antisolvent route has a fully detailed chloride example only: 0.6 mmol CsCl and 0.3 mmol CuCl in 7.5 mL DMSO; 200 µL of precursor solution is injected into 5 mL toluene under vigorous stirring. The precursor-salt ratio is 2:1, distinct from Cs3Cu2Cl5 product stoichiometry.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 7 / printed p. 5521, Experimental, synthesis of Cs3Cu2Cl5 NCs by antisolvent method

canonical_links.relation: source-scoped context; no physical-batch identity inferred

facts.label: DMSO
facts.value: 7.5 mL stock volume; 200 µL aliquot injected.

notes: General method is described at room temperature under ambient conditions; no numeric setpoint, injection rate, or stirring rpm is reported.

paragraphs: The separate hot-injection preparation makes Cs-oleate from 1.2 g Cs2CO3, 3.75 mL OA and 45 mL ODE; the reaction charge is 10 mL ODE and 0.45 mmol CuCl, with 1 mL dried oleylamine and 1 mL dried OA.

items.title: Inkjet ink and substrate treatment
paragraphs: Ink formulation is 40 mg liquid-crystal monomer in 0.4 mL dichlorobenzene plus 0.1 mL purified NC IPA solution. The monomer identity/formula and dichlorobenzene isomer are not specified. Silicon is cleaned sequentially in 10% Micro-90, DI water, acetone and IPA for 20 min each, then treated with the named fluorosilane.

items.title: Room-temperature antisolvent family
paragraphs: The main text describes DMSO precursor solution injected into a nonpolar antisolvent at room temperature under ambient conditions. The detailed chloride example uses vigorous stirring, followed by centrifugation at 6000 rpm for 5 min; discard the supernatant and redisperse in IPA. Other compositions do not inherit the chloride charge quantities.

canonical_links.relation: source-scoped context; no physical-batch identity inferred

facts.label: Product workup
facts.value: Discard supernatant and redisperse in IPA.

notes: Cs3Cu2I5 and CsCu2I3 use IPA as antisolvent in the described examples.

items.title: Hot-injection route
paragraphs: For the separate chloride route, Cs-oleate preparation uses vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h, then N2 to 150 °C until reacted. The reaction mixture is degassed under vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h, returned to N2, raised to 160 °C, and receives 6 mL Cs-oleate preheated to 100 °C; quench after 5 s in ice-water. Purification uses two stated 6000 rpm, 5 min centrifugation steps.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 7 / printed p. 5521, Experimental, hot-injection method

canonical_links.relation: source-scoped context; no physical-batch identity inferred

facts.value: 120 °C vacuum 1 h; N2 to 150 °C until reaction; reaction degas 120 °C vacuum 1 h; reaction at 160 °C.

facts.label: Injection/quench
facts.value: 6 mL stock preheated to 100 °C; quench after 5 s.

notes: This procedure is specific to Cs3Cu2Cl5; no route ancestry or common physical batch is inferred.

items.title: Chloride crystal structure
paragraphs: Figure 1a and the main text assign orthorhombic Cmcm Cs3Cu2Cl5 with a=15.4510(3) Å, b=8.75935(16) Å, and c=8.68517(15) Å. Cu+ is described as disordered between two tetrahedrally chloride-coordinated sites. Detailed refinement tables/coordinates are SI-dependent and remain unreviewed.

paragraphs: The chloride NCs are described as spherical with diameter 2.68 ± 0.80 nm; the accompanying “(30%)” is undefined. HRTEM spacing is about 1.74 Å, consistent with (424). Mean diameters reported for Cs3Cu2Br5, Cs3Cu2I5 and CsCu2I3 are 2.98, 3.61 and 2.86 nm, without main-text uncertainty.

items.title: Absorption, emission and lifetime context
paragraphs: The absorption edge is described near 275 nm with an approximately 4.4 eV gap statement; the paper separately reports DFT gaps around 2.3 eV for Cs3Cu2Br5 and about 0.3 eV lower for Cs3Cu2Cl5. These remain distinct measured/optical and calculated contexts. Figure 3 lifetime range is 0.12–98 µs without composition-mapped endpoints; Figure 5 gives illustrative chloride comparisons of about 98 µs (ligand-free) and 110 µs (OA-capped).

items.title: Self-trapped-exciton emission
paragraphs: The authors interpret the broad, strongly Stokes-shifted emission and microsecond-scale decays in the context of self-trapped excitons. Their model describes free carriers becoming self-trapped through strong electron–phonon interactions, followed by slow radiative decay. This is a mechanistic interpretation, not a directly observed intermediate state.

items.title: Oleic-acid passivation interpretation
paragraphs: The authors report stronger PL intensity and longer lifetime for OA-capped NCs in their comparison and interpret this as partial passivation of trap states, reducing nonradiative recombination. The comparison is not crosswalked to a named synthesis batch.

items.title: Possible causes of PL loss in solution
paragraphs: For solution samples, the authors suggest PL loss may relate to NC aggregation or surface oxidation of Cu+ to Cu2+. They report no noticeable XRD structural change after UV excitation in humid air for 1 h and infer that bulk crystalline phase formation is unlikely to explain the PL loss. These alternatives are not distinguished by the reported comparison.

items.title: Printed-array stability interpretation
paragraphs: The authors report that the printed chloride array remains brightly emissive for longer than 24 h in air and suggest slow oxidation may occur without additional device packaging or NC surface treatment. This is the reported printed-film context; it does not identify the original NC synthesis batch.
